- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak at 1.5–2x recent high to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.11) and model is rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment unit.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 2+ consecutive days), apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.0% of forecast from next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows strong positive momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.23+), model often overreacts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to offset overconfidence.  
- If model forecast is > 1.5% above recent 7-day average, flag for lag correction — reduce by 0.5–1.0% for next 2–3 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.
